text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident detected: high SLO burn for /api/generate (5m window). burn_rate=42% — paging criteria hit. Auto-page sent to #eng-oncall at 2098765432

maya: saw the page, I'm on it. looking at grafana now.

ton y: thanks, maya. quick context: prod traffic spike from partner X around 10:05. might be request pattern causing long tails.

lina: I'm pulling traces for the last 20m. adding query to see 99th latency per model.

alex: FYI customers A/B tests were scheduled; they might be ramping. tagging @growth.

maya: heartbeat — we're seeing KV cache miss spikes on the serving nodes. RTT to kv-store jumped from ~2ms to ~40ms for ~3m.

samir: any errors in runtime logs?

maya: some OOM-ish GC churn on a few pods, but nothing explicit. primary signal is SLO-burnalert: multi-window 5m > 30%. paging threshold as configured.

lina: posted a quick trace snippet: ```
span: runtime.forward
model: redwood-medium-v2
duration_p95: 1.2s
kv_miss: true
```

maya: mitigation idea: temporarily raise paging threshold to avoid noisy pages while we stabilize cache backend. propose: 5m->60%, 1h->15% (keep longer window stricter).

tony: I'd rather avoid changing production paging mid-incident unless we can document rollback. But we're getting a lot of churn. paging->oncall is expensive.

samir: alternative: adjust routing policy to fallback to smaller model variant for requests above length X. That would lower token compute and reduce pressure. Can we flip a rollout?

alex: rollout sounds safer. Can we do a canary 10% shift to small-model fallback for the last 15m requests?

maya: we can push a routing override via the console: policy={"fallback_model":"redwood-small-v1","percent":10}. Doing it now in staging first then prod.

incident-bot: deploy-started by maya at 2098765447: routing-override-canary

lina: confirm: metrics on the canary look good — latency down ~18% for routed requests, kv miss rate unchanged for others.

maya: canary verified. rolling to 30% now.

incident-bot: deploy-complete at 2098765458: routing-override percent=30

samir: after 30% rollout, burn rate dropped to 22% in 5m, and 1h window still at 12%. Looks promising.

tony: great. given that, I don't think we should change paging thresholds. Instead: follow-up items to reduce alert noise and tune SLO windows.

maya: Agreed. proposed post-incident action items: 1) add a multi-window alert that requires both 5m>30% AND 1h>10% before paging. 2) create dashboards split by model variant and routing policy. 3) add a temporary backlog alert for KV store latency.

lina: tiny nit: the boolean AND will reduce pages but might delay paging for real issues. Suggest: paging if 5m>60% OR (5m>30% AND 1h>10%). That keeps sensitivity for spikes but reduces noise for transient blips.

samir: I like Lina's expression. It's basically two-tier: immediate hard spikes page, sustained mid-level burn pages only if longer-window corroborates.

alex: add to that: on-call playbook should include 'check routing overrides' and 'check KV ops dashboard' as first two steps. Saves time.

maya: documenting now. Also adding a short-lived runbook snippet to the incident channel.

incident-bot: note created 2098765466 -> /incidents/2098765432/notes

tony: customer impact check — any error reports or support tickets?

alex: I scanned support queue: three priority-low tickets referencing slow responses; no elevated error rates in API.

maya: internal estimate: <0.1% of requests exceeded SLA during spike window, primarily for long-sequence generate calls. No major revenue impact.

lina: for follow-up engineering work: we should instrument per-request KV cache hit tag and add a Grafana panel showing hit-rate vs p99 latency by model. Also schedule a capacity test for cache backend.

samir: i'll own the routing policy changes and tests. lina you'll own dashboards. maya i'll leave runbook + postmortem draft to you. tony can you own the alert rule change PR?

tony: yes, will put up a PR with the new multi-window AND/OR logic, include rollback steps and a simulated alert test.

maya: timeline: PR + dashboard changes by EOD tomorrow, postmortem draft by Friday.

alex: thanks team. quick retrospective note: autoscaling didn't help here because the KV backend was the bottleneck — need cross-team capacity planning.

incident-bot: incident resolved: SLO burn back under thresholds at 2098765478. incident closed pending postmortem.

maya: closing notes: no paging change for now. implement Lina's rule and dashboards. action owners confirmed. I'll kick off the postmortem doc.
